results.why: K26 scores exactly the explicit numbered-enumeration formatting of contributions/components that T01 asks for, judging layout rather than content.

The nearest candidates (K04, K10, K20, K24, K33) all score general numeric/benchmark-figure density, which strictly contains percentage counting as one sub-case and would score speedups, counts and raw scores that T02 ignores.
No candidate scores the parenthetical '(e.g./i.e./such as)' habit; K30 is about author-year citations in parentheses, a different property.
K50 is a near-verbatim count of named benchmarks/datasets, and K48 counts the same class of externally named resources, so both would produce essentially T04's per-abstract scores.

K40 and K47 touch the opening move but score accessibility of motivation and early-vs-late arrival framing respectively, not specifically whether the first sentence is a generic field-importance platitude.
No candidate scores the advertising of experiment/dataset counts; K20/K24 fold such counts into overall numeric density and K46 scores resource-deliverable framing instead.
All three score visible unrendered LaTeX/markup residue (commands, math delimiters, escapes, footnotes) as pure surface residue, matching T07's property directly.
No candidate scores efficiency-register vocabulary (efficient, lightweight, scalable, fast, low-cost).
No candidate scores the question-posed-and-answered rhetorical structure; K39 scores conformity to the problem-gap-method-results template, a different structural property.
K34 scores exactly the density of promotional adjectives, adverbs and emphatic claims regardless of justification, the same register T10 counts.
K07 scores explicit priority/originality assertions ('first', 'to our knowledge', 'unprecedented') without judging their truth, which is T11's property.
No candidate scores membership in the graph/GNN subfield; K35 covers applied real-world domains and K06/K11/K37 cover trendy LLM-era vocabulary.
